title: How CodeWalk works, in six stops
regenerateHint: Regenerate a short (6-step) English walk of how CodeWalk works — schema, walk loading, the host/webview protocol, jumping to code, anchor checking, and the URI handler — aligned to the current HEAD, with anchors copied verbatim and a 3-question quiz.

steps.title: A walk is just JSON that points at real lines
steps.narration:
Everything you are looking at right now comes from one `.codewalk.json` file. Each step names a **file** and a **line range** — that's it. No plugin API, no generator lock-in: any AI or any human can write one.

This type is the product's only external contract, which is why it lives in a single place and every field carries docs.

terms.explanation: A guided path through code: ordered steps, each tied to a file and line range, plus a closing quiz. Stored as JSON under `.codewalk/` and committed with the repo, so it travels with the code it explains.

steps.title: The extension finds every walk in `.codewalk/`
steps.narration:
When the panel opens, the extension host scans `.codewalk/`, reads every file in parallel and validates each one.

A broken file is **still listed** (falling back to its filename) instead of silently disappearing — so the reader can click in and see what's wrong.

steps.title: Host and panel only talk through messages
steps.narration:
The side panel is a sandboxed web page; it can't open files or touch the editor. So the two halves talk through typed messages defined in this one file.

The host is the source of truth: it decides which step you're on and sends `stepChanged`; the panel just renders.

terms.explanation: An isolated browser page VS Code embeds in a panel. It has no access to the VS Code API — only `postMessage`. That boundary is why this protocol exists at all.

steps.title: Jumping to code without stealing your keyboard
steps.narration:
This is what just happened on your screen: the file opened and the lines were selected and centered.

The key detail is `preserveFocus: true`. Without it, focus would land in the editor after the first jump and the arrow keys would stop moving you through the walk.

steps.title: Knowing when the code has moved on
steps.narration:
Code changes; walks don't update themselves. Each step stores an **anchor** — the exact text it was written against.

- Same text at the same lines → matched
- Same text found once elsewhere → the step **follows it** to the new lines
- Not found, or found twice → flagged **stale**, never guessed

terms.explanation: A verbatim copy of the step's source lines at the time the walk was written. Comparing it with the current file is how CodeWalk tells "the code moved" from "the code changed".

steps.title: Any AI agent can open a walk for you
steps.narration:
An agent that just generated a walk can hand it straight to you with one URI:

`vscode://properworkstudio.codewalk-reader/open?walk=…&step=0`

That's how this demo was opened. Next: the quiz — reading isn't the same as understanding.

quiz.question: Why does jumping to code use `preserveFocus: true`?
options: So the arrow keys keep driving the walk after the first jump
So the file opens in preview mode
optionExplanations: Right: focus stays on the CodeWalk panel, so the next arrow key still means "next step".
Wrong: it has nothing to do with speed — it only decides who holds keyboard focus.
Wrong: preview mode is controlled by `preview: false`, a separate option.

quiz.question: A step's code moved 20 lines down but is otherwise unchanged. What does CodeWalk do?
options: Follows the anchor to the new lines
Highlights the old line numbers anyway
optionExplanations: Wrong: stale is only for text that is gone or appears more than once.
Right: the anchor text is found exactly once elsewhere, so the step shifts to it.
Wrong: that is the failure anchors exist to prevent.

quiz.question: Why can't the side panel open files by itself?
options: It is a sandboxed webview with no VS Code API — it has to ask the host
Opening files is too slow from the panel
optionExplanations: Right: the webview only has `postMessage`; the host does every file and editor operation.
Wrong: speed is not the reason — the panel has no access at all.
Wrong: the format only describes steps; this is a platform boundary.
